Subject: Acme POC: scope, success criteria, and next steps

Thanks Jared and Priya — great call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps to get the POC kicked off: 

Recap
- Goal: Validate Redwood inference throughput and cost savings for Acme search and summarization flows (avg doc size ~1.2k tokens).
- Key stakeholders: Jared (Product), Priya (AI/ML), Sagar (Procurement).
- Timeline target: 3-week POC starting week of Mar 8, aiming for decision by end of March.

Proposed success criteria (preliminary)
1) Latency: 95th percentile < 450ms for single-request QA queries at 4 concurrent users.
2) Cost: projected token cost <= 60% of Acme's current baseline (approx estimate shared on call).
3) Quality: precision on our labeled sample set >= 88% (Priya to confirm metric).
4) Reliability: no more than 1% error rate over test traffic, and KV cache hit rate >= 30%.

Immediate next steps
- I will send a POC plan with responsibilities and assets by Thu 3/5. (Marcus/Dev to confirm test harness requirements.)
- Priya: share a 200-500 sample labeled set and current baseline metrics (quality & cost) by EOD Wed 3/4.
- Sagar: share any standard NDA/procurement timelines that would impact start date.

Attachments: Acme-Executive-Summary-2026-03-02.docx (topline doc we referenced).

Marissa

Subject: Re: Acme POC: scope, success criteria, and next steps

Thanks Marissa — that looks good. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Latency: 450ms P95 is reasonable for the smaller queries; for larger doc summarization flows we may need to agree on a separate target or a two-tier success criterion. Priya and I will map which endpoints fall into which bucket.
- Quality metric: we'll share a labeled sample set (~300 records) by EOD Wed 3/4. Priya will confirm the evaluation script we want used.
- Procurement: Sagar — we typically need a one-page SOW and our security checklist completed before we push infra changes. Any chance you can share a sample SOW and the SOC2 report?

Also, if we start the week of Mar 8, we expect the first integration sprint to be light (sandbox + test data ingestion). Can you confirm Redwood's expected involvement (hours/week) so we can align calendars?

Jared

Subject: Acme POC: formal plan & owners (attached)

Hi all — attaching the formal POC plan (ACME-POC-Plan-2026-03-05.pdf) that maps success criteria, evaluation plan, timelines, and owners. Summary below: 

POC scope (3 weeks)- Week 0 (prep, Mar 8): data ingest & sandbox setup; deliverable: test dataset loaded and basic API connectivity validated. Owner: Dev Patel (Redwood) / Priya (Acme).
- Week 1 (integration & smoke tests, Mar 15): run baseline traffic, measure latency & error rates; deliverable: weekly status report & sample outputs. Owner: Marcus Lin (Redwood) / Priya (Acme).
- Week 2 (quality & cost analysis, Mar 22): run evaluation suite against labeled set, compare cost projections; deliverable: evaluation report + recommendation. Owner: Marcus Lin (Redwood) / Jared (Acme).

Success criteria (finalized)
- Latency P95: <450ms for QA queries; two-tier target for summarization (P95 < 1200ms).
- Cost: <=60% of current baseline for productionized path OR clear quantification if not met.
- Quality: Precision >= 88% on labeled set; detailed metrics in evaluation report.

Evaluation plan
- Redwood to run evaluation harness (script included in attachment) and provide raw outputs + aggregated metrics.
- Acme to run a parallel evaluation on their baseline for apples-to-apples comparison.

Ownership & calendar
- Redwood SEs (Marcus/Dev): 6-8 hours/week across the three weeks for integration and tuning.
- Marissa (AE): weekly sync + exec updates (30–60 min).
- Acme: point persons Priya (ML) and Jared (Product) to own labeled set and acceptance sign-off.

Procurement & security
- Marissa: attaching our SOC2 summary and sample SOW in Drive link. Sagar — happy to run through the checklist; Marcus can join for any technical security questions.

Next immediate asks
1) Priya: share labeled set by EOD 3/6 if possible (we can accept a partial set to start).
2) Sagar: confirm procurement timeline and any required paperwork by Mon 3/9.
3) Marcus/Dev: confirm test harness dependencies in next 24 hours so Acme can provision a sandbox.

Thanks — plan attached.

--
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Acme POC: formal plan & owners (attached)

Looping in a couple technical details: 

- Sandbox requirements: Acme should provide S3-compatible test bucket with role-based access (we can use temporary creds). Prefer data partitioned by topic so we can test per-flow latency.
- Test harness: we'll run the Redwood eval harness (attached script). It needs a sample of 200 warmup queries + 1k steady-state requests for latency profile. If Priya can share sharded datasets, we'll schedule the runs to mirror expected production traffic patterns.
- KV cache: recommend enabling prefix caching for repeated document retrievals; this will materially improve P95 for QA flows. We'll include cache-hit metrics in weekly report.

I'll be available Mon/Tue next week for the initial sandbox validation (30–60 minutes).

Marcus
